messages:
erin: Heads-up — I want to propose a change to the spot-backed autoscaler behavior after last week's cold-start spike. brief: add a lightweight "prewarm probe" + conservative surge cap tweaks.
erin: We saw multiple inference pods stuck pending for >90s when spot nodes got reclaimed, then the autoscaler overshot and we incurred expensive on-demand fallbacks.
max: Can you sketch the triggers?
erin: Yeah. Rough idea:
- scale-out trigger: pending_pods >= 2 for 20s OR avg_queue_ms > 120 for 15s
- prewarm probe: allocate 1x "prewarm" pod per AZ when scale event detected, run small gpt-serve warmup script (30s) to populate KV cache
- surge cap: cap scale burst to +30% of desired replicas for 60s, then allow further growth with longer cooldown
jas: Interesting. Prewarm pods would be cheaper than full replica? how do we ensure they actually help?
erin: Prewarm runs a light-weight init: loads model weights with quantized kernels, sets up KV cache with a synthetic prefix, then exits or promotes itself to real replica if load persists. Saves ~70% of init time vs cold pod on same node.
sri: Where do we put the config? autoscaler supports annotations right now. Example config snippet:
```yaml
apiVersion: autoscaling.redwood/v1
kind: SpotAutoscalerPolicy
metadata:
  annotations:
    rw/scale-trigger: \"pending>=2:20s, queue>120ms:15s\"
spec:
  surgePercent: 30
  surgeWindow: 60s
  prewarm:
    enabled: true
    perAZ: 1
    probeCmd: [\"/usr/local/bin/warmup\", "--kv-prefix", "prewarm"]
  cooldown: 180s
```
max: Looks good. Couple things to watch: 1) We must prevent prewarms from creating excessive spot churn. 2) Ensure prewarm pod tolerations don't force placement on scarce GPUs.
jas: For 1) maybe limit prewarm attempts per node to 1 per 10m. For 2) set nodeAffinity to prefer idle-gpu taints but fall back to mixed-pool nodes.
infra-bot: Notice: cluster-a: spot-rebalance event at 1905123540 — 12 nodes reclaimed in us-west2.
erin: That event is exactly why I'd like to gate aggressive scale-out in single AZ. Proposal: add AZ-hedging multiplier: when reclaimed_nodes_in_AZ>5 in last 10m, reduce surgePercent to 10 and enable cross-AZ allocation.
sri: Cost tradeoffs? more cross-AZ = higher egress for KV cache sync, but reduces on-demand fallback. We should model it.
max: We should also tune cooldowns per model size. Bigger models -> longer cooldown to let KV caching amortize. Maybe a simple function: cooldown = base * (model_gb / 8).
jas: Also add an interruption-probe signal: if node preempt probability > 0.6 (from spot-price model), mark pool as low-confidence and stop prewarm for that pool.
erin: Agreed. I'd like to run a canary: cluster-a small pool with these settings for two weeks. Measure: p99 cold-start, cost delta, on-demand fallbacks.
max: Assigning tasks: jas -> update autoscaler controller to support prewarm lifecycle (ETA 4d). sri -> run cost simulation and produce delta table (ETA 2d). erin -> bake warmup container + probe script.
jas: I'll add guards: max-prewarm-per-node and per-pool inhibition when preempt_prob>0.6.
infra-bot: autoscaler-bot deployed v0.9.2 to staging at 1905123620
autoscaler-bot: Runbook note: if canary raises on-demand usage > 2x baseline, autoscaler will auto-disable prewarm and notify #oncall.
erin: Thanks — let's sync Friday for initial metrics. :thumbsup:
